why_relevant: Statutory financial-statement register for all Slovak accounting entities, searchable by IČO/name/LEI. Confirms that an actor exists, is active and at what scale – essential for filtering the actor list down to entities big enough to run meaningful tenders, and for sizing vendors named in award notices.

Largest Slovak ICT industry association; its members are precisely the systems integrators and IT vendors that bid on bank and public-sector technology tenders. Supplies the supply-side half of the A2 actor universe that financial licence registers cannot provide.

Peak employers' body whose members span banking, insurance and the IT sector, and which includes sectoral associations as members. Useful as an association-of-associations pointer that surfaces smaller sector bodies not otherwise indexed.

~218-member body of CFOs, treasurers, banks, financial institutions and explicitly 'financial and software providers/consultants'. Its membership and event sponsors expose the corporate-treasury and treasury-software vendor layer relevant to payments procurement.

source_name: EBA EUCLID – Credit Institutions Register & PSD2 Payment Institutions Register (SK filter)
why_relevant: EU-level cross-check on the Slovak actor universe: lists SK-authorised credit and payment institutions plus inbound passporting entities that serve Slovakia from other Member States and therefore never appear in an SK-only register. Closes the cross-border blind spot in the actor list.

Commercial aggregator combining ORSR, registeruz, VAT and debtor lists into one entity profile. Fastest way to enrich an actor name with IČO, revenue, ownership and links to public-sector contracts; used here to confirm association legal identities (e.g. Slovak FinTech Association IČO 51910497).

source_name: Banky.sk – zoznam bánk na Slovensku (consumer portal directory)
why_relevant: Non-official but conveniently structured directory of Slovak banks and of the SBA itself, useful as a quick alias/brand-name table (trading names vs legal names) for text-matching bank names in tender notices.

Leading SK business weekly; covers banking sector deals, bank IT/digitalisation spend, state IT tenders and who-won-what narratives that never surface as structured notices. Historically the outlet that names suppliers behind large financial-sector contracts.
Daily economic newspaper; routinely reports contested state tenders, banking-sector regulation and vendor selections, including finance-ministry and state-bank IT procurement disputes.

Denník E is the business vertical of Denník N; it runs sustained coverage of state IT spending ('Slovensko už v IT utopilo miliardu'), procurement scandals and bank/fintech business stories — strong for politically sensitive or delayed tenders.

source_name: Denník N – live tag feed 'Verejné IT zákazky / Slovensko.sk'
why_relevant: A curated running topic feed aggregating short items on public IT contracts; acts as a pointer to actors, contract names and controversies to snowball into ÚVO/CRZ lookups.

The most consistent SK outlet covering state IT tenders in technical detail (evaluation criteria, vendor protests, ÚVO decisions) plus banking apps, instant payments and digital identity. Weak-signal source ahead of formal award notices.

B2B IT trade press covering enterprise/banking IT projects, integrator wins and vendor announcements — often the only public trace of private-bank core-system or payment-platform deals that have no procurement notice.

source_name: TOUCHIT.sk – technology magazine (+ BrandIT press-release service)
why_relevant: Covers Slovak bank digital products, instant payments rollout, fintech programmes (e.g. Tatra banka/RBI FinTech Scouts). Its brandit.touchit.sk arm republishes bank press releases verbatim — useful as an early, machine-readable vendor/partnership signal.

Specialist SK financial trade title with keyword taxonomy pages (e.g. 'platobné služby'); covers payment-service providers, PSD2/instant payments, bank supplier and M&A news. Good structured entry points for topic monitoring.
Business magazine profiling fintech/payment companies and bank executives; occasional deal and vendor-strategy detail plus interviews that reveal procurement intentions before tenders.

Major news portal with a dedicated investigative team (the desk Ján Kuciak worked on); produces corruption/procurement investigations that expose contested awards, ownership chains and conflicts of interest around state contracts.

Non-profit investigative newsroom monitoring organised crime, corruption and links to institutions; publishes deep dives on public contracts and beneficial ownership relevant to who really wins state financial/IT contracts.
Open discussion forum where IT professionals debate specific tenders before/while they run — surfaces vendor complaints, specification criticism and insider context weeks ahead of media coverage.
Law-firm-authored commentary and interviews on Slovak public procurement and financial-services regulation; useful for interpretation of contested award procedures and ÚVO/court practice.
Dedicated practitioner portal with expert/lawyer articles on procurement practice, ÚVO decisions and methodology — helps interpret how notices for financial/IT services are structured and challenged.

source_name: Wolters Kluwer SR – journal 'Verejné obstarávanie – právo a prax'
why_relevant: Bi-monthly professional journal written by procurement lawyers and practitioners; authoritative on procedural changes and case law that shape how financial/IT tenders are run and contested.

Law-firm blog explaining procurement rules and advising both contracting authorities and bidders; representative of the law-firm blog layer that flags rule changes affecting bank/payment service tenders.

source_name: JUDr. Ondrušek – právny blog (transparency / public-sector partners register)
why_relevant: Lawyer blog focused on public-sector transparency and the Register partnerov verejného sektora — the disclosure regime that reveals beneficial owners of firms winning state financial/IT contracts.
